analysis.title: Employment Situation: Job gains crush expectations, unemployment rate falls, in very strong October jobs report
key_insights: October nonfarm payrolls rose 165k versus a consensus expectation of 70k. August and September were revised up by a combined 84k, bringing the three-month moving average to 137k per month.

Job growth was broad. Private payrolls rose 159k in October. Professional and business services added 70k, the fastest pace since 2022. Construction hiring was also strong and PNC ties it at least in part to the AI capex buildout.

The unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, matching the year-to-date low and down from a peak of 4.5% last November. Labor force participation rose to 61.9% and the employment-to-population ratio to 59.3%, both improving for a third straight month.

Average hourly earnings rose 0.37% m/m and 3.1% over the past year, stronger than anticipated. PNC says professional and business services hiring (generally higher-wage jobs) may have skewed the monthly print through compositional effects. It sees the broader wage trend as weakening or stabilizing at a relatively non-inflationary level.
Aggregate payroll income rose at a 5.8% annualized pace in October, which PNC calls a good proxy for nominal income growth.

PNC estimates the economy needs about 50k jobs per month to hold the unemployment rate steady. If job gains stay above 100k, it expects further declines in the unemployment rate by year-end and into 2027.

PNC says the report changes its view on the labor market. Hiring, the unemployment rate and wages all pointed the same way, and it thinks the report cleared the high bar set by jitters over the AI buildout.
PNC's base case is that the Fed hikes in December and March. It considers market odds of a December hike, near 80%, appropriate.

sector_views.rationale: Employment added 70k in October, the fastest monthly pace since 2022.
Nonresidential construction employment was strong, very likely tied in part to the AI capex buildout.
A large portion of jobs are still being added in healthcare. Private education and health added 53k in October.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Far above the 70k consensus. Broad-based strength that PNC says changes its view on the labor market.
Consensus expectation that the actual print beat by 95k.
Upward revisions lifted the three-month average to 137k per month.
A very strong pace compared with the roughly 50k needed to hold unemployment steady.
Job growth was concentrated in the private sector and broad across industries.
Matches the year-to-date low, down from a 4.5% peak last November. The decline came from hiring, not lower participation.
Stronger than anticipated, partly from compositional effects of high-wage professional services hiring.
PNC sees the broader wage trend as relatively non-inflationary.

tension_points.bull_case: Average hourly earnings rose 0.37% m/m and 3.1% y/y, stronger than anticipated, and aggregate payroll income grew 5.8% annualized, which supports a December hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Part of the monthly wage strength may reflect compositional effects from higher-wage professional and business services hiring. The broader wage trend has been weakening or stabilizing at a relatively non-inflationary level.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If job gains stay above 100k, PNC expects the unemployment rate to keep falling by year-end and into 2027.
